article_text:
James McAvoy has starred in films including “Speak No Evil,” “Atonement” and “X-Men: First Class,” but he recently revealed the “only” film he still consistently receives residuals from is M. Night Shyamalan’s 2016 horror “ Split .”

“You get the odd check for, you know, a couple 100 quid here or sometimes you get checks for, like, 25 cents and you’re like, ‘It literally costs more to post this than it did for me to cash it,’” McAvoy said during a recent episode of the Happy Sad Confused podcast. “But the only one that really consistently pays me is ‘Split.’”

Related Stories

Why ‘Office Space’ Actor Richard Riehle Was the Quintessential Actor’s Actor (Guest Column)

Marjoe Gortner, Preacher and Actor Who Was Subject of Oscar-Winning Doc and Appeared in 'Earthquake,' 'Falcon Crest,' Dies at 82

“I think it was made for like $6 million or something like that? And let’s say they spent 30 advertising it. In our first weekend, we made 40, so we were in profit,” McAvoy continued. “Our first residual check came at the end of the first weekend. It was bonkers.”

Popular on Variety

In “Split,” three girls are kidnapped by a man with a diagnosed 23 distinct personalities (McAvoy). “They must try to escape before the apparent emergence of a frightful new 24th,” per the film’s official description. Anya Taylor-Joy, Haley Lu Richardson and Jessica Sula starred alongside McAvoy. The film, which cost just $6 million to make, went on to gross $138.29 million domestically and $140.16 million internationally for a $278.45 million worldwide total.

McAvoy also spoke about Shyamalan and his experience working with the director.

“I very consciously took from many of the directors that I worked with, and subconsciously as well, but the thing I took away from him is his preparedness,” McAvoy said. “He made that film, and [sequel] ‘Glass,’ on incredibly modest budgets, and very focused on how he would maximize his day and maximize his shots and maximize what he got out of the story by just being incredibly well-prepared and being able to share that and communicate that with the crew.”

title_original: Emerging Arab Directors Given a Pathway Toward Filmmaking Careers by Expanded Pitching Platform at Sharjah Film Festival
editorial_title_zh: 阿联酋沙迦国际儿童和青少年电影节扩大项目创投平台，为新兴阿拉伯导演开辟电影职业发展道路
editorial_excerpt_zh: 阿联酋沙迦国际儿童和青少年电影节（Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth）迎来第13届，其创投平台在第二年进一步扩大。今年有6个项目入选，多于首届时的3个。此次扩大是沙迦国际电影节（SIFF）……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿联酋沙迦国际儿童和青少年电影节（Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth）迎来第13届，其创投平台在第二年进一步扩大。今年有6个项目入选，多于首届时的3个。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此次扩大是沙迦国际电影节（SIFF）努力为新兴电影人开拓培训和展映之外的发展路径的一部分。正如电影节总监谢赫·贾娃希尔·宾特·阿卜杜拉·阿勒卡西米（Sheikha Jawaher bint Abdullah Al Qasimi）在今年电影节开幕前接受《综艺》杂志采访时所说，学会如何拍电影只是其中一部分，“要把这部电影制作出来并让观众看到，则是完全不同的挑战。”今年的项目汇聚了来自整个阿拉伯世界及海外 diaspora 的电影人，核心目标是在沙迦及更广泛地区寻找资金和制作合作伙伴。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相关报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/David-Bowie.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "大卫·鲍伊", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "布雷特·摩根执导的大卫·鲍伊沉浸式音乐会体验《Stage》将在柏林电影节世界首映", "links": [{"text": "David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience ‘Stage’ From Brett Morgen to World Premiere at Berlin Film Festival", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/david-bowie-immersive-concert-experience-stage-berlin-1236931930/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "以下是今年创投环节展示的6部短片项目：", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《The Black Hole》（Mike Mo Elsherif，美国。制片人：JohnBen Lacy）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴勒斯坦裔美国电影人迈克·穆·埃尔谢里夫（Mike Mo Elsherif）执导的《The Black Hole》讲述了一位居住在美国的加沙难民在寻找加沙家人的线索时患上了一种神秘疾病。埃尔谢里夫将这部电影形容为“对我们的身体如何在人的一生中储存和处理创伤的深刻探索，凸显了身体感官与情感体验之间的紧密联系。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该片是一部短片三部曲的一部分。第一部《Maqluba》在入选伍德斯托克、黑星（BlackStar）和埃尔古纳（El Gouna）等电影节后，在沙迦国际电影节（SIFF）的阿拉伯短片竞赛单元上映；而目前处于后期制作阶段的《Goodbye Habibi》则由巴勒斯坦电影实验室（FilmLab Palestine）、伊斯兰奖学金基金（Islamic Scholarship Fund）、多哈电影学院（Doha Film Institute）和肯塔基艺术委员会（Kentucky Arts Council）资助。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该项目目前处于融资阶段，是通过总部位于路易斯安那州的非营利组织502 film旗下的编剧实验室“前廊实验室”（The Front Porch Lab）以及写作机构“新和谐项目”（The New Harmony Project）开发完成的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《The Black Hole》部分通过私人融资，目前正寻求在沙迦获得更多资金，以便于2027年冬天在肯塔基州路易斯安那开机拍摄。埃尔谢里夫将该项目描述为“对一名巴勒斯坦人内心的心理学研究，他正在努力应对自己每天目睹的心碎与非人化对待”，也是在祖国满目疮痍之中寻求疗愈的过程。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Kot Kot Kot》（Boubaker Boukhari，阿联酋）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Kot Kot Kot》讲述了一个小女孩艰难应对母亲离世的故事。她的父亲送给她一只小鸡，她把它抚养长大成一只母鸡，并与它产生了极深的感情，不料有一天它突然消失了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影源于布哈里（Boukhari）童年时母亲给他讲的一个故事，他多年来几乎已经忘得精光，直到几年后他的小侄子在一次家庭聚会上重新讲起这个故事。“他声音里的情感与惊奇让我意识到，这是一个值得再次讲述的故事，”布哈里告诉《综艺》杂志。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部由阿联酋独立制作的项目目前正在制作中，此前为自筹资金，目前正寻求资金以完成后期制作，尤其是音乐、声音设计、音效和录音方面。布哈里还签约了突尼斯联合制片人阿莱丁·阿布·塔勒布（Alaeddin Abou Taleb，来自Key Production Films），其作品包括曾获迦太基电影节（Carthage Film Festival）金塔尼特奖（Tanit d’Or）的定格动画短片《Diaspora》。该片计划于2026年底完成。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "插画师娜迪亚·齐拉诺娃（Nadia Zilanova）的国际作品包括曾为《纽约时报》及各大出版社供稿，她最近加入了该项目，负责以“独特的视觉风格”创作和为电影背景上色。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《The Last Call》（Saleh Mohammed，阿联酋）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "常驻阿联酋的电影人萨利赫·穆罕默德（Saleh Mohammed）的《The Last Call》从一通来自某个已被遗忘记忆的号码的意料之外的电话开始，带领其主角踏上一段穿越过去、未解情感以及未答之问的情感旅程。穆罕默德表示，这部电影探讨了“我们没有说出口的话，以及直到失去才懂得去珍惜的时刻。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这位导演将自己电影的视觉手法描述为“克制的”，让电影得以反思“单一时刻如何改变人生，以及我们有时只有在某人离去后才认出其存在价值的方式。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "剧本已完成，项目正处于前期制作阶段，外景勘测正在进行中，接下来将进行选角和剧组组建。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "穆罕默德正在寻求资金和赞助，以及潜在的联合制片人和行业合作伙伴，以推动电影进入制作阶段。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "穆罕默德说：“在这个时刻保持沟通的世界里，真正的连接有时反而是我们最容易忽视的。”他还利用沙迦国际电影节（SIFF）在电影最终上映前与各大电影节和发行商建立联系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "穆罕默德的职业生涯始于剧场演员和导演，他还在哈利德·阿尔·马哈茂德（Khalid Al Mahmood）执导的今年电影节开幕影片《The Mangrove House》中联合主演。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Lucky Shot》（Salah Al Hadhrami，阿联酋。编剧：Dalila Al-Dar’iya）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿曼电影人萨拉赫·阿尔·哈德拉米（Salah Al Hadhrami）的《Lucky Shot》围绕阿姆贾德（Amjad）展开，这是一个来自工人阶级社区的男孩，他对足球的热爱激起了他摆脱平庸处境的生活梦想。一次意料之外的转折迫使他在这些雄心壮志与可能改变他未来的诱惑之间做出选择。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部由阿曼电影人、编剧兼演员达莉拉·阿尔-达里娅（Dalila Al-Dar’iya）编剧的12-15分钟叙事短片目前正在开发中，已开始接洽潜在演员。该独立项目尚未落实制作资金，目前正在沙迦及地区其他地方寻找资助者和联合制片人，暂定于2027年开机，具体取决于资金落实情况。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我相信简单的故事也能承载最深刻的人性讯息，”阿尔-哈德拉米说道。对这位导演而言，这部电影与其说讲的是足球本身，不如说讲的是当一个意想不到的机会成为“真正的考验”时的那一刻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿尔-哈德拉米表示，最核心的目标是“讲一个超越地理和文化界限、能与观众情感产生共鸣的真实故事。我们希望找到相信这一讯息并助力将这部电影搬上银幕的伙伴。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我的萨曼叔叔”（“Saman 3my”）\n（阿尔朱里·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·阿尔扎鲁尼 [Aljouri Abdelaziz Alzarooni]，阿联酋。创意制片人：沙哈德·阿尔·阿里 [Shahad Al Ali]）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿联酋编剧兼导演阿尔朱里·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·阿尔扎鲁尼的《我的萨曼叔叔》讲述了三个年轻人前往参加他们期待已久的叔叔婚礼的途中发生的故事。新郎的年龄与他们相仿，感觉更像个表兄弟，他派他们去跑个短腿，结果却演变成了一连串的奇遇，导致三人面临错过整个婚礼的风险。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部喜剧短片目前处于开发阶段，尚未落实资金或签约制作公司。阿尔扎鲁尼正在SIFF上寻找资金和制作合作伙伴，并在摄影、声音和后期制作等领域寻求合作者。她表示，路演已经引起了潜在合作伙伴的兴趣，目前正在进行洽谈。这位年轻的导演表示，潜在合作伙伴对该项目“展现阿曼（注：应为阿联酋，照原文语义）叙事的新颖独特视角”表现出了强烈热情。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“《我的萨曼叔叔》扎根于阿联酋家庭的天然幽默、人际关系和日常经历，我想以一种能够与各地观众产生共鸣的方式将这种真实感搬上银幕，”阿尔扎鲁尼说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "随着资金筹措工作的持续推进，阿尔扎鲁尼也在关注未来可能来自潜在发行商、广播机构、流媒体平台和行业导师的支持。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“番茄商贩”（“Tomato Merchant”）\n（索拉亚·法尔扎内 [Thoraya Farzaneh]，阿联酋。制片人：赛义德·穆萨维 [Sayed Mousavi]）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "常驻阿联酋的电影人索拉亚·法尔扎内凭借《番茄商贩》迎来导演处女作，影片讲述了一位老人在宁静的街区卖了一整天番茄，在所有番茄卖光之前坚决不肯离开的故事。随着人们一次次试图说服他回家，其坚持背后的原因也逐渐浮出水面。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "法尔扎内过去几年一直担任副导演并从事剧本创作，她表示自己一直等到感觉准备就绪时才执导自己的故事。“我觉得这是迈出这一步、与世界分享我的故事的正确时刻。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部独立短片已获得由沙迦阿尔卡西米基金会（Al Qasimi Foundation）支持的RAK艺术基金（RAK Art Fund）的资金支持，而作为该电影节母机构的FANN - 媒体发现平台（FANN – Media Discovery Platform）将在其SIFF路演结束后提供后期制作支持。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《番茄商贩》目前处于前期制作阶段，定于11月上旬在阿联酋开机，目标是在1月完成制作。法尔扎内正借助SIFF为成片探索电影节和发行机会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "制片人赛义德·穆萨维表示：“这部电影提醒我们，善意往往始于选择保持耐心的简单决定。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Tomato-Merchant.jpg?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "《番茄商贩》剧照，由索拉亚·法尔扎内提供", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The 13th edition of the UAE’s Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is expanding its pitching platform for its second iteration. Six projects were selected this year, up from the three that took part during its inaugural program."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The expansion is part of SIFF’s effort to build a pathway for emerging filmmakers beyond training and exhibition. As festival director Sheikha Jawaher bint Abdullah Al Qasimi told Variety ahead of this year’s edition, learning how to make a film is only part of the equation, “getting that film produced and seen is a completely different challenge.” This year’s projects bring together filmmakers from across the Arab world and diaspora, with the principal goal of finding financing and production partners from Sharjah and beyond."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Related Stories"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/David-Bowie.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "David Bowie", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience ‘Stage’ From Brett Morgen to World Premiere at Berlin Film Festival", "links": [{"text": "David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience ‘Stage’ From Brett Morgen to World Premiere at Berlin Film Festival", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/david-bowie-immersive-concert-experience-stage-berlin-1236931930/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Here are the six short film projects presented at this year’s pitching sessions:"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The Black Hole” (Mike Mo Elsherif, U.S. Produced by JohnBen Lacy)"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Palestinian-American filmmaker Mike Mo Elsherif’s “The Black Hole” follows a Gazan refugee living in the U.S. who develops a mysterious illness as he searches for answers about his family in Gaza. El Sherif describes the film as a “visceral exploration of the complex ways in which our bodies store and process trauma throughout our lives, highlighting the deep connection between physical sensations and emotional experiences.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The film is part of a trilogy of shorts. The first installment, “Maqluba,” screens in the Arabic short films competition at SIFF following stops at Woodstock, BlackStar and El Gouna, while “Goodbye Habibi,” now in post-production, was financed by FilmLab Palestine, the Islamic Scholarship Fund, the Doha Film Institute and the Kentucky Arts Council."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Currently in the financing stage, the project was developed through screenwriting lab The Front Porch Lab, under Louisville-based nonprofit 502 film, as well as The New Harmony Project, a writing organization."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Partially privately financed, “The Black Hole” is seeking further funding in Sharjah ahead of a winter 2027 shoot in Louisville, Kentucky. Elsherif describes the project as “a psychological study of a Palestinian grappling with the heartbreak and dehumanization he witnesses every day,” and a search for healing amid the devastation of his homeland."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Kot Kot Kot” (Boubaker Boukhari, UAE)"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Kot Kot Kot” follows a young girl grappling with the loss of her mother. Her father gives her a chick that she raises into a hen with which she grows deeply attached, only for it to suddenly disappear one day."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The film grew from a story Boukhari’s mother told him as a child, which he had largely forgotten until his young nephew recounted it years later at a family gathering. “The emotion and wonder in his voice made me realize that this was a story worth telling again,” Boukhari tells Variety ."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Currently in production, the independently-produced UAE project has been self-financed and is seeking funding to complete post-production, particularly in music, sound design, sound effects and sound recording. Boukhari has also signed Tunisian co-producer Alaeddin Abou Taleb of Key Production Films, whose credits include the Tanit d’Or-winning stop-motion short “Diaspora” at the Carthage Film Festival. Completion is planned by the end of 2026."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Illustrator Nadia Zilanova, whose international work includes commissions for the New York Times and publishing houses, recently joined the project to create and color the film’s backgrounds “in a distinctive visual style.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The Last Call” (Saleh Mohammed, UAE)"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "UAE-based filmmaker Saleh Mohammed’s “The Last Call” begins with an unexpected phone call from a number connected to a forgotten memory, sending its protagonist on an emotional journey through the past, unresolved feelings and unanswered questions. Mohammed says the film explores “the things we leave unsaid and the moments we fail to appreciate until they are gone.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The director described the visual approach of his film as “restrained,” allowing the film to reflect “on how a single moment can change a life and how we sometimes recognize the value of someone’s presence only after they are gone.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The screenplay is complete and the project is in pre-production, with location scouting underway and casting and crew assembly next."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mohammed is seeking financing and sponsorship, as well as potential co-producers and industry partners to help move the film into production."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“In a world where communication is constant, genuine connection can sometimes be the thing we overlook most,” Mohammed says. He is also using SIFF to build relationships with festivals and distributors ahead of the film’s eventual release."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mohammed, who began his career as a theater actor and director, also co-stars in Khalid Al Mahmood’s “The Mangrove House,” the opening film of this year’s festival."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Lucky Shot” (Salah Al Hadhrami, Oman. Screenwriter Dalila Al-Dar’iya)"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Omani filmmaker Salah Al Hadhrami’s “Lucky Shot” centers on Amjad, a boy from a working-class neighborhood whose passion for football fuels dreams of a life beyond his modest circumstances. An unexpected turn of events forces him to choose between those ambitions and temptation that could change his future."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Written by Omani filmmaker, writer and actor Dalila Al-Dar’iya, the 12-15 minute narrative short is in development, with initial approaches made to potential cast members. The independent project has yet to secure production financing and is seeking backers and co-producers in Sharjah and elsewhere in the region, with a tentative 2027 shoot dependent on funding."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I believe that simple stories can carry the profoundest human messages,” Al Hadhrami says. For the director, the film is less about football itself than the moment when an unexpected opportunity becomes “a true test.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The goal, above all, Al Hadhrami shares, is “to tell an authentic story that transcends geographical and cultural boundaries, one that resonates with the audience’s emotions. article_text:
The 13th edition of the UAE’s Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is expanding its pitching platform for its second iteration. Six projects were selected this year, up from the three that took part during its inaugural program.

The expansion is part of SIFF’s effort to build a pathway for emerging filmmakers beyond training and exhibition. As festival director Sheikha Jawaher bint Abdullah Al Qasimi told Variety ahead of this year’s edition, learning how to make a film is only part of the equation, “getting that film produced and seen is a completely different challenge.” This year’s projects bring together filmmakers from across the Arab world and diaspora, with the principal goal of finding financing and production partners from Sharjah and beyond.

Related Stories

David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience ‘Stage’ From Brett Morgen to World Premiere at Berlin Film Festival

Here are the six short film projects presented at this year’s pitching sessions:

“The Black Hole” (Mike Mo Elsherif, U.S. Produced by JohnBen Lacy)

Palestinian-American filmmaker Mike Mo Elsherif’s “The Black Hole” follows a Gazan refugee living in the U.S. who develops a mysterious illness as he searches for answers about his family in Gaza. El Sherif describes the film as a “visceral exploration of the complex ways in which our bodies store and process trauma throughout our lives, highlighting the deep connection between physical sensations and emotional experiences.”

The film is part of a trilogy of shorts. The first installment, “Maqluba,” screens in the Arabic short films competition at SIFF following stops at Woodstock, BlackStar and El Gouna, while “Goodbye Habibi,” now in post-production, was financed by FilmLab Palestine, the Islamic Scholarship Fund, the Doha Film Institute and the Kentucky Arts Council.

Currently in the financing stage, the project was developed through screenwriting lab The Front Porch Lab, under Louisville-based nonprofit 502 film, as well as The New Harmony Project, a writing organization.

Partially privately financed, “The Black Hole” is seeking further funding in Sharjah ahead of a winter 2027 shoot in Louisville, Kentucky. Elsherif describes the project as “a psychological study of a Palestinian grappling with the heartbreak and dehumanization he witnesses every day,” and a search for healing amid the devastation of his homeland.

“Kot Kot Kot” (Boubaker Boukhari, UAE)

“Kot Kot Kot” follows a young girl grappling with the loss of her mother. Her father gives her a chick that she raises into a hen with which she grows deeply attached, only for it to suddenly disappear one day.

The film grew from a story Boukhari’s mother told him as a child, which he had largely forgotten until his young nephew recounted it years later at a family gathering. “The emotion and wonder in his voice made me realize that this was a story worth telling again,” Boukhari tells Variety .

Currently in production, the independently-produced UAE project has been self-financed and is seeking funding to complete post-production, particularly in music, sound design, sound effects and sound recording. Boukhari has also signed Tunisian co-producer Alaeddin Abou Taleb of Key Production Films, whose credits include the Tanit d’Or-winning stop-motion short “Diaspora” at the Carthage Film Festival. Completion is planned by the end of 2026.

Illustrator Nadia Zilanova, whose international work includes commissions for the New York Times and publishing houses, recently joined the project to create and color the film’s backgrounds “in a distinctive visual style.”

“The Last Call” (Saleh Mohammed, UAE)

UAE-based filmmaker Saleh Mohammed’s “The Last Call” begins with an unexpected phone call from a number connected to a forgotten memory, sending its protagonist on an emotional journey through the past, unresolved feelings and unanswered questions. Mohammed says the film explores “the things we leave unsaid and the moments we fail to appreciate until they are gone.”

The director described the visual approach of his film as “restrained,” allowing the film to reflect “on how a single moment can change a life and how we sometimes recognize the value of someone’s presence only after they are gone.”

The screenplay is complete and the project is in pre-production, with location scouting underway and casting and crew assembly next.

Mohammed is seeking financing and sponsorship, as well as potential co-producers and industry partners to help move the film into production.

“In a world where communication is constant, genuine connection can sometimes be the thing we overlook most,” Mohammed says. He is also using SIFF to build relationships with festivals and distributors ahead of the film’s eventual release.

Mohammed, who began his career as a theater actor and director, also co-stars in Khalid Al Mahmood’s “The Mangrove House,” the opening film of this year’s festival.

“Lucky Shot” (Salah Al Hadhrami, Oman. Screenwriter Dalila Al-Dar’iya)

Omani filmmaker Salah Al Hadhrami’s “Lucky Shot” centers on Amjad, a boy from a working-class neighborhood whose passion for football fuels dreams of a life beyond his modest circumstances. An unexpected turn of events forces him to choose between those ambitions and temptation that could change his future.

Written by Omani filmmaker, writer and actor Dalila Al-Dar’iya, the 12-15 minute narrative short is in development, with initial approaches made to potential cast members. The independent project has yet to secure production financing and is seeking backers and co-producers in Sharjah and elsewhere in the region, with a tentative 2027 shoot dependent on funding.

“I believe that simple stories can carry the profoundest human messages,” Al Hadhrami says. For the director, the film is less about football itself than the moment when an unexpected opportunity becomes “a true test.”

The goal, above all, Al Hadhrami shares, is “to tell an authentic story that transcends geographical and cultural boundaries, one that resonates with the audience’s emotions. We hope to find partners who believe in this message and will help bring the film to the screen.”

“My Uncle Saman” (“Saman 3my”) (Aljouri Abdelaziz Alzarooni, UAE. Creative Producer Shahad Al Ali)

Emirati writer-director Aljouri Abdelaziz Alzarooni’s “My Uncle Saman” follows three young men on their way to their uncle’s long-awaited wedding. The groom, who is close enough in age to feel more like a cousin, sends them on a quick errand that turns into a string of misadventures, leaving the trio at risk of missing the wedding altogether.

The comedy short is in development and has yet to secure financing or attach a production company. Alzarooni is seeking financing and production partners at SIFF, along with collaborators in areas including cinematography, sound and post-production. She says the pitch has already generated interest from potential partners, with discussions now underway. The young director says potential partners expressed strong enthusiasm for the project’s “fresh and distinctive approach to Emirati storytelling.”

“‘My Uncle Saman’ is rooted in the natural humour, relationships, and everyday experiences of Emirati families, and I want to bring that authenticity to the screen in a way that audiences everywhere can connect with,” Alzarooni says.

Alzarooni is also eyeing eventual support from potential distributors, broadcasters, streaming platforms and industry mentors as her search to secure financing continues.

“Tomato Merchant” (Thoraya Farzaneh, UAE. Produced by Sayed Mousavi)

UAE-based filmmaker Thoraya Farzaneh makes her directing debut with “Tomato Merchant,” about an elderly man who spends his day selling tomatoes in a quiet neighborhood and refuses to leave until they are all sold. As repeated attempts are made to persuade him to go home, the reason for the insistence gradually becomes clear.

Farzaneh, who has spent the past several years working as an assistant director and writing scripts, says she waited until she felt ready to direct a story of her own. “I feel this is the right moment to take that step and share one of my stories with the world.”

The independent short has received funding from the RAK Art Fund, supported by the Sharjah-based Al Qasimi Foundation, while FANN – Media Discovery Platform, the parent organization of the festival, will provide post-production support following its SIFF pitch.

Now in pre-production, “Tomato Merchant” is set to shoot in the UAE in early November, with completion targeted for January. Farzaneh is using SIFF to explore festival and distribution opportunities for the finished film.

Producer Sayed Mousavi says, “This film reminds us that kindness often begins with the simple choice to be patient.”
